_source: PyCQA/bandit examples/ tree — 91 files hand-curated by the bandit maintainers as their own test corpus. Each filename names the weakness it demonstrates; this manifest maps file → expected fendix category for the subset fendix is supposed to detect.
_methodology: category_counts. Each expectation is 'fendix should flag at least one finding matching <title_re> in <category> when scanning bandit/examples/'. Files that demonstrate weaknesses outside fendix's scope (TLS, crypto, XML, network-config) are NOT expected — that's not a fendix miss.
_files_not_in_fendix_scope: ciphers.py / cipher-modes.py / crypto-md5.py / hashlib_new_insecure_functions.py — weak crypto (fendix has Semgrep coverage if installed; not in core engine)
ssl-insecure-version.py / no_host_key_verification.py / unverified_context.py — TLS misconfig (not in scope)
xml_*.py — XML external entity / pulldom (not in scope)
assert.py / nosec.py / nonsense*.py / okay.py / new_candidates-*.py — bandit-internal test cases, not security weaknesses
requests-missing-timeout.py / requests-ssl-verify-disabled.py — operational hygiene, not in core engine

expected.note: os_system.py uses a literal-string argument — fendix _cmdi_arg_is_dangerous correctly suppresses literals; not a fendix miss

os-popen.py has both literal-string (correctly suppressed) AND os.popen4(some_var) tainted at the bottom — fendix should flag the latter. Currently miss because os.popen2/3/4 aren't sinks (only os.popen). Real engine gap.
paramiko_injection.py — fendix has no paramiko-specific rule today (permissive)

urlopen.py demonstrates urllib.request but with literal-string URLs. Once urllib SSRF sink is added, this still won't fire (literals are correctly suppressed). The real urllib SSRF coverage is graded by Juliet's bad_02_urllib_urlopen (tainted case).
eval.py + exec.py — fendix's eval detector is permissive on the bandit examples (which use rare patterns)
deserialisation family — permissive because fendix's deser sinks are AST-pattern-narrow
